editorialNote: Focused KB for Alzheimer disease. The modern pipeline splits into (1) anti-amyloid antibodies (lecanemab approved 2023, donanemab approved 2024, aducanumab withdrawn 2024), (2) symptomatic cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine, and (3) next-wave anti-tau / anti-inflammatory / GLP-1 programs. Any research output that discusses AD but omits lecanemab AND donanemab is AI slop.

Blood pressure control (SPRINT-MIND suggests target <120 mm Hg systolic)
Vaccinations (flu, shingles — herpes zoster vaccination associated with reduced dementia incidence in Welsh natural experiment)

items.title: Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease (CLARITY-AD)
items.authors: van Dyck CH, Swanson CJ, Aisen P, et al.
items.summary: Phase 3 RCT of lecanemab (Leqembi, Eisai/Biogen) in 1,795 patients with early symptomatic AD. Primary endpoint CDR-SB change at 18 months was -0.45 points favoring lecanemab (27% slowing of decline, P<0.001). ARIA-E in 12.6% of lecanemab patients (2.8% symptomatic); ARIA-H in 17.3%. Basis for full FDA approval July 2023.

keyPassages.quote: Lecanemab reduced clinical decline at 18 months as measured by the CDR-SB, with a between-group difference of -0.45 (95% CI, -0.67 to -0.23; P<0.001).
Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities with edema or effusions (ARIA-E) occurred in 12.6% of the lecanemab group and 1.7% of the placebo group.

items.title: Donanemab in Early Symptomatic Alzheimer Disease (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2)
items.authors: Sims JR, Zimmer JA, Evans CD, et al.
items.summary: Phase 3 RCT of donanemab (Kisunla, Lilly) in 1,736 patients. iADRS change at 76 weeks favored donanemab (difference 3.25 points in low/medium-tau population, P<0.001). 35-36% slowing of decline. ARIA-E 24% (6% symptomatic); three treatment-related deaths. Basis for FDA approval July 2024.

keyPassages.quote: In the low/medium tau population, the adjusted mean change from baseline at 76 weeks on the iADRS was -6.02 in the donanemab group and -9.27 in the placebo group (difference, 3.25; 95% CI, 1.88 to 4.62; P<0.001).
ARIA-E occurred in 24.0% of donanemab-treated participants and 2.1% of placebo-treated participants; symptomatic ARIA-E occurred in 6.1% versus 0.1%.

items.title: Biogen discontinues commercial sale of Aduhelm (aducanumab) — January 2024
items.summary: Biogen announced in January 2024 that it would discontinue development and commercialization of aducanumab (Aduhelm), the controversial anti-amyloid antibody that received FDA accelerated approval in June 2021 over the objection of the advisory committee. Access to trial patients was transitioned; commercial product withdrawn. Patients who have been on aducanumab must discuss switching to lecanemab or donanemab with their neurologist.

keyPassages.quote: Biogen will discontinue the development and commercialization of ADUHELM and terminate the ENVISION clinical study.

items.title: LEQEMBI (lecanemab-irmb) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.summary: Indication: treatment of Alzheimer's disease in patients with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia stage with confirmed amyloid pathology. Dose: 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks. Boxed warning for amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA). Pre-treatment MRI required; MRI at doses 5, 7, and 14. Homozygous APOE ε4 carriers have highest ARIA risk.

keyPassages.quote: ARIA can occur spontaneously in patients with AD. ARIA-H associated with lecanemab can occur at any time and is usually asymptomatic, although serious and life-threatening events, including intracerebral hemorrhages, have been reported.

items.title: KISUNLA (donanemab-azbt) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.summary: Indication: AD in patients with MCI or mild dementia stage with confirmed amyloid pathology. Dose: 700 mg IV q4wk x3 then 1400 mg IV q4wk. Can be stopped when amyloid plaques cleared (amyloid PET below threshold) — unique among anti-amyloid agents. Boxed warning for ARIA. Literature warns against use in ApoE ε4 homozygotes without special counseling due to highest ARIA risk.

keyPassages.quote: KISUNLA treatment can be stopped based on reduction of amyloid plaques to minimal levels on amyloid PET imaging.

items.title: Dementia prevention, intervention, and care: 2024 report of the Lancet standing Commission
items.authors: Livingston G, Huntley J, Liu KY, et al.
items.summary: Updated Lancet Commission on dementia prevention. Now identifies 14 modifiable risk factors accounting for ~45% of dementia risk worldwide: hearing loss, hypertension, smoking, obesity, depression, physical inactivity, diabetes, low social contact, excessive alcohol, traumatic brain injury, air pollution, lower education, vision loss (new), and high LDL (new). This is the evidence base for most lifestyle recommendations.

canonicalFacts.claim: Lecanemab (Leqembi) is FDA-approved (full approval, July 2023) for early symptomatic AD with confirmed amyloid pathology; slows CDR-SB decline by ~27% over 18 months.
Donanemab (Kisunla) is FDA-approved (July 2024) for the same stage; slows iADRS decline by ~35% in low/medium-tau patients. It can be discontinued once amyloid plaques clear on PET.
Aducanumab (Aduhelm) was withdrawn from the US market by Biogen in January 2024. It is NOT a current treatment option.
APOE ε4 homozygotes have the highest risk of ARIA with anti-amyloid therapy and should receive extra counseling before initiation.

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Treat hearing loss (amplification/hearing aids) — largest single modifiable population-attributable risk for dementia in the Lancet Commission.
Strict blood-pressure control (target systolic ≲120-130 mm Hg) — SPRINT-MIND.
Avoid anticholinergic-burden medications (diphenhydramine, oxybutynin, TCAs); review with pharmacist.
Treat obstructive sleep apnea if present.

redFlags: Physicians generally caution against starting anti-amyloid therapy (lecanemab or donanemab) without confirming amyloid pathology (CSF Aβ42/40 ratio or amyloid PET) — labels require it.
Literature warns against anti-amyloid therapy in patients on anticoagulants — CLARITY-AD and TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 data suggest dramatically elevated intracerebral hemorrhage risk.
Physicians generally caution against prescribing aducanumab (Aduhelm) — Biogen withdrew it from the market in January 2024.
Evidence does not support relying on cognitive supplements (Prevagen, ginkgo biloba, coconut oil) — no RCT evidence of benefit; Prevagen was subject to FTC action for deceptive advertising.

pipelineDrugs.name: Lecanemab
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody targeting soluble amyloid-β protofibrils
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA full approval July 2023 for early symptomatic AD with amyloid confirmation
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: First anti-amyloid antibody with full FDA approval. 27% slowing of decline at 18 months. Omitting this is AI slop.

pipelineDrugs.name: Donanemab
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: IgG1 monoclonal antibody targeting pyroglutamate-modified Aβ (N3pG) on plaques
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA approval July 2024 for early symptomatic AD
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Second anti-amyloid antibody approved. Can be discontinued once amyloid clears on PET — unique.

pipelineDrugs.name: Aducanumab
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: IgG1 monoclonal antibody targeting aggregated amyloid-β
pipelineDrugs.status: Accelerated approval June 2021; Biogen WITHDREW from US market January 2024
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Historically first of class; withdrawn. Patients and families still ask — must be addressed as no-longer-available.

pipelineDrugs.name: Donepezil
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: First-line symptomatic therapy across AD severity. Modest benefit on cognition; does not alter disease course.

pipelineDrugs.name: Rivastigmine
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Transdermal patch reduces GI side effects vs oral.

pipelineDrugs.name: Galantamine
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: AChE inhibitor + nicotinic receptor allosteric modulator
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Third cholinesterase inhibitor; dual mechanism theoretically advantageous but outcomes similar.

pipelineDrugs.name: Memantine
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Add-on to cholinesterase inhibitor in moderate-severe AD.

pipelineDrugs.name: Gantenerumab
pipelineDrugs.status: GRADUATE I & II phase 3 FAILED (November 2022); program discontinued
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: High-profile failure. Patients and clinicians still ask about it — must be addressed as failed.

pipelineDrugs.name: Solanezumab
pipelineDrugs.status: A4 (preclinical AD prevention) FAILED primary endpoint 2022 (NEJM); development halted
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: The preclinical-AD prevention story with solanezumab is negative and shapes interpretation of all subsequent prevention trials.

pipelineDrugs.name: Blarcamesine
pipelineDrugs.status: Phase 2b/3 ATTENTION-AD completed; regulatory filings underway in EU 2024-2025
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Oral small-molecule in late-stage development; mechanism distinct from anti-amyloid class. Patients ask about this frequently.

pipelineDrugs.name: Semaglutide
pipelineDrugs.status: evoke and evoke+ phase 3 trials in early AD; readout expected 2025
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Most consequential repurposing trial in AD. Positive readout would reshape the field.

pipelineDrugs.name: Remternetug
pipelineDrugs.status: TRAILRUNNER-ALZ 1 / 3 phase 3 ongoing (preclinical and early symptomatic AD)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Lilly's follow-on to donanemab aiming at convenient SC dosing.

excludedAgents.name: Aducanumab (Aduhelm)
excludedAgents.reason: Withdrawn from US market by Biogen in January 2024. No longer commercially available. Any AD output recommending aducanumab as a current option is out of date.

excludedAgents.name: Ginkgo biloba for dementia prevention
excludedAgents.reason: GEM study (Ann Intern Med 2008, JAMA 2008) showed no effect on dementia incidence in >3,000 older adults followed ~6 years. Not recommended by any current guideline.

excludedAgents.name: Prevagen (apoaequorin)
excludedAgents.reason: No credible RCT evidence of cognitive benefit. Subject of FTC enforcement action 2017 for deceptive advertising.

excludedAgents.name: Coconut oil / MCT oil for AD
excludedAgents.reason: No high-quality RCT evidence. Popular on patient forums; not recommended.

excludedAgents.name: Stem cell clinics offering IV MSC infusions for AD
excludedAgents.reason: No peer-reviewed efficacy data for AD. FDA warning letters to multiple operators. Patient-safety concern.
